docs.404.body: The page does not exist, has moved, or has not been published.
docs.home.body: Use JavaScript generator functions to coordinate concurrent work, wait at explicit points, and make cancellation and recovery predictable.
docs.home.description: Documentation, Flow Explorer, and API Map for shajara.
docs.home.hero.tagline: Async work with clear ownership and predictable cleanup.
docs.home.title: Structured concurrency for JavaScript
explorer.examples.all-results.descriptio: all(...) collects parallel routine results into one future.
explorer.examples.all-results.guide.futu: wait(pageData) observes both results together, preserving the order from all(...).
explorer.examples.all-results.guide.work: renderDashboard calls all(...), starting loadUser and loadSettings.
explorer.examples.all-results.title: All Results
explorer.examples.bounded-channel.descri: Bounded channel capacity lets receivers apply backpressure to senders.
The draft send is accepted before the channel fills.
queueBatches creates a capacity-one channel and shares the receiver with writeBatches.
writeBatches receives later values as the waiting sends are accepted.
review and publish arrive while the buffer is full, so their sends wait.
explorer.examples.bounded-channel.title: Bounded Channel
explorer.examples.failure-driven-cancell: A child scope failure cancels the remaining work before the caller receives ScopeError.
launchCampaign calls branch(...), opening the sendCampaign child scope.
When sendEmailBatch throws, the sendCampaign scope cancels the sleeping work.
The sendCampaign scope contains sendCampaign, sendEmailBatch, and refreshAudience.
After the scope closes, launchCampaign receives ScopeError at the branch(...) call.
explorer.examples.first-result.descripti: race(...) returns the first successful value after canceling the remaining work.
explorer.examples.first-result.guide.rac: loadProfile calls race(...), starting readCache and fetchNetwork.
explorer.examples.first-result.guide.win: readCache wins; race(...) cancels fetchNetwork before returning the profile.
explorer.examples.first-result.title: First Result
explorer.examples.fork-join.description: spawn(...) forks work and wait(...) joins the returned futures.
explorer.examples.fork-join.guide.fork: loadPage starts loadHeader and loadSidebar as separate processes.
explorer.examples.fork-join.guide.join: loadPage waits for both futures before returning the combined page result.
explorer.examples.fork-join.title: Fork Join
explorer.examples.future-settlement.desc: One routine waits on a future, and another routine settles it later.
explorer.examples.future-settlement.guid: receiveSmsCode settles smsCode with the received code.
verifyPhoneNumber waits at wait(smsCode) until that settlement arrives.
explorer.examples.recovery-boundary.desc: guard(...) routes a resumable(...) failure to a recovery handler.
explorer.examples.recovery-boundary.guid: publishListing enters guard(...), and reviewListing waits at resumable(...).
scanPhotos throws while reviewListing is waiting.
approveManually handles the failure at the guard boundary.
The recovery value returns to reviewListing as approval.
Futures and channels are owned by the scope that creates them.
openSession creates ticket and updates inside the openSession scope.
When the openSession scope closes, it cancels ticket and revokes updates.
When branch(...) returns, the openSession scope has closed and resumeCheckout receives the handles.
Later wait(...) and tryReceive(...) observe the canceled and revoked states.
explorer.examples.scope-owned-work.descr: Work owned by a child scope must finish before the caller continues.
explorer.examples.scope-owned-work.guide: publishArticle calls branch(...), opening the commitArticle child scope.
commitArticle returns published before updateSearchIndex finishes.
updateSearchIndex is spawned inside the commitArticle scope.
publishArticle continues from branch(...) only after updateSearchIndex finishes.
explorer.examples.scope-owned-work.title: Scope-Owned Work
explorer.examples.single-spawn.descripti: spawn(...) starts one separate process and returns a future for it.
explorer.examples.single-spawn.guide.cal: submitOrder returns order accepted while sendReceiptEmail continues.
explorer.examples.single-spawn.title: Single Spawn
explorer.home.title: Flow Explorer
